text: Kant's 'Copernican revolution' in philosophy consists in the claim that:
choices: Objects of experience must conform to the mind's a priori forms of intuition and categories, rather than the mind simply conforming to objects
The mind passively mirrors a fully mind-independent reality
All our ideas are faint copies of prior sense impressions
The self is nothing but a bundle of perceptions with no unifying subject
explanation: Kant reversed the assumption that knowledge must conform to pre-given objects: instead, objects of experience must conform to the mind's own a priori structures (space, time, and the categories). Option 1 is the pre-Kantian 'passive mirror' picture he rejected; option 2 is Hume's empiricism and option 3 is Hume's bundle theory — the very positions the Critique was answering.
